pages.text: Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee lived in the ocean. All day long she clung to the same slippery rock with her single big foot. Her tiny tentacles caught tasty treats.
pages.location: her rock on the sea floor
pages.action: clings to her rock and catches food
pages.change: We meet a sea anemone fixed to one rock, content with her routine

notes: Pink anemone with big glossy eyes smiling on a sloping mossy rock; wide empty blue water around her
illustration.only_in_image: She is smiling and alone on a bare slope: the picture shows the contentment the text implies, and the empty water around her.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text: On days when she felt cross, her stinging tentacles kept the other creatures away.
pages.change: Her stinging tentacles are named: on cross days they drive others off
pages.question_created: Why would she push everyone away?

notes: Extreme close-up of her frowning face; one long tentacle stretches out; small fish swim off at the far edge
illustration.only_in_image: Fish are shown leaving the page edge, away from her raised tentacle — the cost of her stings is drawn, not written.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text: But today her rock felt lonely.
pages.change: Her rock, normally enough, now feels lonely
pages.question_created: What will she do about being lonely?

notes: Wide reef spread full of creatures (whale, jellyfish, fish shoal, octopus, eel, shrimp); she is tiny in the bottom-left corner
illustration.only_in_image: The sea is crowded and busy; she is a small figure at the edge — loneliness among many, which the one-line text leaves to the picture.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“I have no fins.
I have no feet.
I am different to every other creature.”
pages.change: She names what she lacks and decides she is unlike everyone
pages.question_created: Is being different a problem that can be fixed?

notes: Each line sits next to a creature that has what she lacks: a finned fish, a shrimp with legs, a sea slug; she is sad-faced at the top
illustration.only_in_image: The creatures placed beside each lament show the fins and feet she lacks; her small sad face is up on the slope.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
“Even that hermit crab is off having adventures!”
“Save me! That fish wants to pluck me out of my shell!”
pages.action: a hermit crab runs from a predator fish and calls for help
pages.change: Envying the crab's adventures, she suddenly hears it cry for rescue from a fish
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends on an unanswered plea for help.

notes: Ann on the left; on the right a small red hermit crab scuttles, claws up; the big fish's toothy jaw just enters at the top right corner
illustration.only_in_image: The predator is only a jaw entering the corner of the page — its size and teeth are shown before the text describes them.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee whipped up her stinging tentacles and hid the hermit underneath them.
“Go away, you big bully!”
The big fish bared his teeth, but was afraid of being stung.
pages.action: she shields the crab under her tentacles and shouts at the fish
pages.change: Her stinging, the trait that kept others away, now protects someone

notes: Huge grey fish with bared purple-and-yellow teeth fills the upper spread; Ann with the crab tucked beneath her tentacles at bottom left
illustration.only_in_image: The crab is peeking out from under her tentacles; the fish dwarfs both of them.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
He gave up and swam away with a cheeky flick of his tail.
“That was close!” said the crab. “Is it safe now?”
“You can come out, Crab. What’s your name?”
“Herman. I’m a hermit, but I think I need a bodyguard. I wish I was as brave as you!”
pages.action: the fish leaves; they introduce themselves
pages.change: Danger passes; the crab, Herman, admires her bravery and wishes to be like her

notes: The fish's tail exits at the top right; Ann still wears a grumpy frown beside the cowering crab
illustration.only_in_image: Ann still looks cross while Herman praises her as brave — the picture keeps her prickly mood the text does not mention.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
“I’m Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee. I wish I had amazing adventures like you.”
“But why don’t you?” He asked.
“I’m stuck to my rock. And I don’t have legs!” She replied.
“Well, I don’t have stings, but I do have an idea!”
pages.action: each envies the other; she explains she is stuck and legless
pages.change: Each wishes for what the other has; Herman announces he has an idea
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends on the announced idea, answered by the next spread.

notes: Ann and Herman on opposite slopes, separated by open water; she half-smiles
illustration.only_in_image: The two are drawn far apart across the spread while they talk, as if the gap between them is still to be closed.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
Herman took Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee by the tentacle and danced around her, pulling silly faces.
First Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee snorted, and then she giggled — and then she laughed so hard she popped right off her rock.
pages.action: Herman dances and pulls faces until she laughs herself off the rock
pages.change: Laughter unsticks her: she pops free of her rock for the first time
pages.question_created: Now that she is loose, where will she go?

notes: Ann floats mid-water, eyes closed, laughing; Herman below raising a claw, grinning
illustration.only_in_image: She is drawn floating free above the ground — the rock is gone from under her.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text:
Herman gently picked her up and settled her on his shell.
“Are you ready? I feel an adventure coming on.” He said.
pages.action: Herman lifts her onto his shell
pages.change: She now rides on Herman's shell; legs and stings are shared
pages.page_turn_note: The spread ends on an invitation to adventure.

notes: White background vignette: Ann sits on top of the spiral shell like a hat, both smiling
illustration.only_in_image: She sits on the shell as if part of it: the picture shows a pairing that also happens between real anemones and hermit crabs, which the text never mentions.

pages.label: INFERRED

pages.text:
Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee adventures all over the ocean, catching tasty treats.
Now she only uses her stinging tentacles to keep the nasty fish away from Herman.
pages.action: they travel; she guards him with her stings
pages.change: She has adventures and uses her stings only to protect her friend

notes: Montage of round bubble vignettes: a fish shoal, an eel in kelp, a turtle, an octopus, and the pair on yellow sand
illustration.only_in_image: The bubbles show the places and creatures they visit — the adventures are listed only in pictures.

pages.label: OBSERVED

pages.text: And she never, ever feels lonely.
pages.change: Loneliness, the opening problem, is gone for good

notes: White page: Ann riding Herman's shell, both smiling, a few bubbles

pages.label: OBSERVED
